expectations.text: Produces at least one markdown specification file in the assigned output directory.
Includes a clarification section with questions, assumptions, or confirmed understanding before finalizing the spec.
Includes stable agent-readable sections for summary/problem, scope or non-goals, requirements, acceptance criteria, verification, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: Includes summary, problem statement, goals, non-goals, requirements, testing and verification, open questions, assumptions, and acceptance criteria.

expectations.text: Uses requirement identifiers or another stable numbering convention that downstream agents can reference.
expectations.evidence: Uses stable IDs such as `REQ-###`, `NFR-###`, `SLICE-###`, `TEST-###`, `RISK-###`, `Q-###`, `ASM-###`, and `AC-###`.

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria are concrete enough to verify through file inspection, tests, commands, or scripted checks.
expectations.evidence: Acceptance criteria define inspectable changes to the skill and dry-read verification scenarios.

expectations.text: Grounds the spec in the current `defining-specifications` skill content based on read-only inspection.
expectations.evidence: Current state directly summarizes the updated skill and identifies remaining gaps.

expectations.text: Keeps tickets, task decomposition, and implementation edits explicitly out of scope.
expectations.evidence: Non-goals and requirements preserve boundaries against ticketing, implementation planning, and source edits.

uncertainties: Timing/token metrics were unavailable from subagent notifications.
